articles.title: FDA-cleared medical AI rarely tested for real-world benefits

articles.title: More coffee, higher testosterone? This study found a more complicated picture
articles.description: Higher habitual coffee intake was associated with a leaner body composition, lower circulating branched-chain amino acids, and distinct cardiometabolic patterns in 2,264 middle-aged Finnish adults. Hormonal associations differed by sex, with broader testosterone- and SHBG-related patterns in men and more limited SHBG-related changes in women.

articles.title: More than 1,000 genetic switches reveal why female immunity is different
articles.description: More than 1,000 genetic switches behave differently in male and female immune cells, helping explain why women are much more vulnerable to autoimmune diseases such as lupus. Female immune systems appear genetically tuned for stronger inflammatory responses—a powerful defense against infection that may also make dangerous immune misfires more likely.

articles.title: Two distinct types of brain tissue work together to support cognition in older adults

articles.title: WHO Weekly Situation Update on Ongoing Health Emergency Events in South Sudan - Week #33, Date: 10 - 16 Aug 2026
articles.description: Countries: South Sudan, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda Source: World Health Organization Please refer to the attached file. PRIORITY ACTIONS Operationalize the new Tier 1A/1B/1C county framework — prioritize Ezo, Yambio, Juba, Yei, Morobo and Nzara for EVD/BVD IPC supplies, case management capacity and RCCE under the area-based readiness approach. Expedite the ICG application for OCV vaccines for Renk mop-up campaign. Investigate the two new cVDPV1 isolates (Pibor and Juba environment); consider extending the SNID to nationwide NIDs given spread to Pibor and Tonj East. Act urgently on the 23% GAM rate in Jonglei and Akobo West (all 8 facilities closed); provide outreach clinics in IDP areas, restore EPI services, and fast-track supplementary immunization to prevent VPD outbreaks. Restore health services for communities in Akobo West (11 facilities still closed), complete the IRNA in Walgak & Waat, and advance the SNID preparations (25–28 August).
